rows.b: Transistors built from a single layer of molybdenum disulfide, a crystal that is a natural semiconductor unlike graphene. Stacked layers could build 3D chips.
A slim computer that slides into a rack with dozens of siblings, serving websites and files around the clock. It is built for reliability, not looks.
Atomic-scale defects in diamond hold quantum states that survive at room temperature. They sense magnetic fields with exquisite precision as well as compute.
Diamond crystals with single-atom defects hold quantum states at room temperature. They sense magnetic fields atom by atom and can serve as qubits.
A gear machine designed to compute mathematical tables by the method of finite differences, stamping results ready for printing. It used only addition and carriage, never multiplication.
Digital files encoded into synthetic DNA strands store staggering amounts of data in a speck of material. Chemical reactions can also run simple computations on the strands.
